question: Does an independent algorithmic family reproduce the same qualified B0 finite-window endpoint selected population within a predeclared method-parity budget?

source_requirements.native_library_build_and_radial_bank: must match current B0 qualification identity

required_inputs: Exact current B0 c_initial bytes/hash at z=-12; never reuse endpoint state at another time
Qualified operator provider at each requested actual time; at(t) returns S,H,D,Sdot with identity receipt; Sdot must have independently validated provenance
Current baseline endpoint c and selected probability with its existing temporal/operator evidence
Predeclared method_parity_budget and its relation to the global error budget; numerical values must be bound before execution

Fresh resource proposal binding initial nstep, maximum refinement count, exact unique query accounting, ordered qualification ladder/raw attempt cap, wall/RAM/CPU/deadline, stop policy, authorization identity
Common normalized-IVP receipt and each method actual initial state/norm/distance, under a predeclared initial-state allowance.

provider_interface.time_map: z=v*t using the pinned existing trajectory convention
prohibited: silent state renormalization during CF4 propagation

stage_rule.adjacent_pair_raw_qualification_ceiling: 11 times distinct uncached queries unless the actual pinned provider policy differs; any difference requires a newly bound proposal

run_rule: Use only the prebound initial stage count, compare same endpoint and norm; refine by factor 2 only within the fresh approved proposal and only when result could change parity status.
stop_rules: Any provider qualification, source identity, state identity, metric SPD, or independent derivative failure: preserve first failure and stop
No budget or authorization identity: native calls remain zero
No tolerance relaxation after inspecting result
Stop once independent-family difference and component uncertainty enclosures satisfy the predeclared criterion, or resource cap is reached
return_schema: CF4 refinement differences and direct-method difference

current_remaining_blocker.claim: Physical parity within a production-relevant budget
current_remaining_blocker.first_failing_artifact: This contract has no bound qualified time-dependent B0 provider/independent Sdot dataset, state hashes, stage count or parity budget
current_remaining_blocker.minimum_repair: Bind existing B0 source/state identities and qualified provider plus predeclared budget; create fresh narrow run proposal
current_remaining_blocker.already_complete: Whitening derivation, CF4 code, exact synthetic solution, six focused tests, comparison against existing midpoint and direct DOP853
current_remaining_blocker.unverified: Physical stage sampling, physical independent Sdot, real observable parity and production-budget acceptance

common_initial_value_contract.source_state: One exact initial-state byte payload at z=-12 and one exact S0 identity shared by every method.
common_initial_value_contract.normalization_policy: Predeclare the common normalized IVP. Existing midpoint/DOP853 normalize supplied c0; CF4 preserves its supplied norm. Explicitly construct the intended common initial state, record each method actual post-initialization state, and compare them before any trajectory comparison.
common_initial_value_contract.budget_requirement: Predeclare a numerical initial-state discrepancy allowance and include its propagated contribution in the parity error chain. Null budget means no physical launch.
common_initial_value_contract.admission: Reject inconsistent source/state/time/metric identities, nonpositive norms, undeclared normalization or initial distances exceeding the predeclared allowance.
common_initial_value_contract.synthetic_benchmark: Existing analytic initial norm1 result remains valid; a nonunit input is not the same IVP across current methods without this explicit mapping.
